description: Cooperative A\* (CA\*) plans many agents fast by planning them one at a time. Agents take turns in index order; each takes the cheapest path that avoids a shared space-time *reservation table* holding the paths of the agents before it: their vertex at every time, the reverse of each move so no two agents swap, and their goal from their arrival on, for good. The low level is space-time A\* guided by each agent's true distance to its goal, which Silver's *hierarchical* variant (HCA\*) computes with reverse resumable A\*; a distance table per agent gives it here, so this CA\* is HCA\* in the paper's terms. The plan has no quality guarantee, and CA\* is not complete: a finished agent holds its goal forever, so a later agent that must pass it finds no path. Use it as the fast baseline for many agents, or WHCA\* when agents block each other.
